newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Greenpeace protests at nuclear shipment.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Greenpeace protests at nuclear shipment.

text.p: Greenpeace activists chained themselves to a lorry at a Dutch nuclear plant on Tuesday to try to prevent containers of radioactive waste being shipped to Britain's Sellafield reprocessing plant.
A spokesman for the environmental pressure group said about 25 protesters had blocked the path of the empty lorry outside the plant in Dodewaard, southeast Netherlands.
"We have about 10 members chained to the lorry, with others coming in rotation," Greenpeace spokesman Diederik Samsom told Reuters from the scene. "We've certainly disrupted their plans."
He said the lorry had been due to take nuclear waste from Dodewaard to the French port of Dunkirk, where it would join material from elsewhere in Europe for its final destination at Sellafield.
A vessel, the European Shearwater, was waiting at the port and was due to sail for Britain on Wednesday afternoon or Thursday morning, he said.
Frits Bots, spokesman for electricity producer SEP, which runs the Dodewaard plant, said plant officials were liaising with local police to disperse the demonstrators.
He would not say when any shipment of nuclear waste was planned. "We can't give any information about those plans," he said.
But said that since the Dodewaard plant was opened in 1975, some 92 separate shipments of waste had been made to Sellafield where it was still stored, unreprocessed.
"All the material from Dodewaard is being stored at Sellafield. We are waiting our turn for it to be reprocessed," he said.
Dodewaard is due to end electricity production next week, but it has a backlog of nuclear waste to be sent to Britain, Bots added.
